title: Root-projection reduction of finite ramified Tate coefficients
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\geq1$, and put $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For any scheme $T$ on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-pc-scheme], work on $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with constant ring sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Put $Z_T=(\mathbf Z_\ell)_T$, $R_{r,T}=(\mathbf Z/\ell^r)_T$ and $L_T=\varprojlim_{s\geq1}\mu_{\ell^s,T}^{\mathrm{pro}}$, with root projections $p_{r,T}$ and power transitions $P_{r',r}:z\mapsto z^{\ell^{r'-r}}$ [def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf, def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit]. Let $P_T=A_T^{\mathrm{pro}}(1)$ be the prescribed finite pro-etale twist [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], and use sheaf tensors [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product].

There is a canonical reassociation isomorphism $j_T:P_T\xrightarrow{\sim}L_T\otimes_{Z_T}A_T$, taking $(x\otimes b)\otimes a$ to $x\otimes ba$. For every $r\geq1$ with $\ell^rA=0$, the map induced by $p_{r,T}$ is an isomorphism
$$\theta_{r,T}:P_T\xrightarrow{\sim}D_{r,T}:=\mu_{\ell^r,T}^{\mathrm{pro}}\otimes_{R_{r,T}}A_T,\qquad j_T^{-1}(x\otimes a)\longmapsto p_{r,T}(x)\otimes a.$$
For $r'\geq r$ with $\ell^rA=0$ it satisfies $(P_{r',r}\otimes1)\theta_{r',T}=\theta_{r,T}$; thus $P_{r',r}\otimes1:D_{r',T}\to D_{r,T}$ is invertible, and these maps obey the identity and composition equations.

For every scheme morphism $v:T'\to T$, use pro-etale inverse image [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], identifying inverse images of constant rings with the target constant rings. Let $c^v_s:v^{-1}\mu_{\ell^s,T}^{\mathrm{pro}}\to\mu_{\ell^s,T'}^{\mathrm{pro}}$ be the canonical root map adjoint to pullback of units [def-pur-roots-of-unity-inverse-image]. There is a unique map $c^v_L:v^{-1}L_T\to L_{T'}$ with $p_{s,T'}c^v_L=c^v_sv^{-1}p_{s,T}$ for all $s$. Define $b_v:v^*P_T\to P_{T'}$ by transporting $c^v_L\otimes1$ through $j_T,j_{T'}$ and the canonical tensor pullback identifications. Then
$$\theta_{r,T'}b_v=(c^v_r\otimes1)v^*\theta_{r,T}.$$
The maps $c^v_L,b_v$ obey the identity and composition laws under the canonical inverse-image identifications. These assertions concern ordinary tensor products and require only $\ell^rA=0$, with no flatness of $A$ over $\mathbf Z/\ell^r$ and no ramification-index divisibility condition.

proof.text: Give $L_T$ its $Z_T$-action by $(a x)_s=x_s^{a\bmod\ell^s}$; the power transitions respect reduction of the exponent, so this is an action on compatible tuples. In additive module notation, define $j_T((x\otimes b)\otimes a)=x\otimes ba$ and its inverse by $x\otimes a\mapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes a$. The balancing relations make both maps well defined, and their composites are the identity on pure tensors. Sheafify these natural sectionwise formulas. The definition of $P_T$ identifies the first source with the prescribed finite twist.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product: sheaf tensors and associativity; finite twist definition in the cited blueprint

proof.text: The projections $p_{r,T}$ are locally surjective. Indeed, apply lem-pur-twist-root-transitions to every consecutive power map. The general-site abelian epi criterion makes it locally surjective on underlying sets, and the set epi criterion makes it an epimorphism of set sheaves. Given an object $U$ and $u\in\mu_{\ell^r}(U)$, cover $U$ by the affine objects $V_i$ weakly contractible for the full $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ site. On each fixed $V_i$, every consecutive transition is surjective on sections by that precise weak contractibility assertion. Set $x_r=u|_{V_i}$, define $x_s=u|_{V_i}^{\ell^{r-s}}$ for $s<r$, and choose recursively $x_{s+1}$ above $x_s$ for $s\geq r$. This gives a compatible tuple, hence an element of $L_T(V_i)$ with $r$th projection $u|_{V_i}$. All uses are on the full site; no infinite refinement of etale covers is asserted.

source.place: Tag 0990, lemma-proetale-enough-w-contractible; sites.tex Tag 090K, lemma-w-contractible; Kummer transitions from etale-cohomology.tex Tag 03PK

proof.text: Compute the kernel on every object $U$. If $x=(x_s)_s\in L_T(U)$ has $x_r=1$, put $y_s=x_{s+r}$. Since $x_{s+r}^{\ell^s}=x_r=1$, this really belongs to $\mu_{\ell^s}(U)$, and $y_{s+1}^\ell=y_s$. Also $y_s^{\ell^r}=x_s$. Conversely $(\ell^r y)_r=y_r^{\ell^r}=1$ for every $y$. Thus in additive notation $\ker p_r(U)=\ell^rL_T(U)$, with an explicit division map on the kernel, compatible with restrictions.

proof.text: Put $H=L_T\otimes_{Z_T}A_T$, which is killed by $\ell^r$ since $\ell^rA=0$. For local sections $u$ of $\mu_{\ell^r}$ and $a$ of $A_T$, choose local lifts $x$ of $u$ by step 2 and set $B(u,a)=x\otimes a$. Two lifts differ by $\ell^r y$ by step 3, so their tensors differ by $y\otimes\ell^ra=0$. The local outputs therefore glue uniquely and commute with restrictions. Addition in either input follows by choosing lifts $x+x'$ and by distributivity of the tensor. For fixed $a$ this is an additive map to $H$ on the slice site, so lem-pur-torsion-sheaf-constant-module (2) makes it $R_{r,T}$-linear; both source and target are killed by $\ell^r$. Consequently $B(cu,a)=B(u,ca)$ for local $c\in R_{r,T}$, and $B(u,aa')=a'B(u,a)$. The universal property of the sheaf tensor gives an $A_T$-linear map $D_{r,T}\to H$. Conversely $x\otimes a\mapsto p_r(x)\otimes a$ is $Z_T$-balanced, since the action in step 1 projects to exponent reduction. Both composites are identity: on $x\otimes a$ choose the lift $x$, and on $u\otimes a$ use any local lift of $u$. The pure-tensor determination statement proves equality of the resulting sheaf maps. Compose $H\cong D_{r,T}$ with $j_T$ to obtain precisely $\theta_{r,T}$. No exactness of tensoring with $A$ was used.

proof.text: For $r'\geq r$, apply both sides of the asserted transition equation to $j_T^{-1}(x\otimes a)$. They give respectively $x_{r'}^{\ell^{r'-r}}\otimes a$ and $x_r\otimes a$, which agree by compatibility of the tuple. Pure tensors determine the maps, so $(P_{r',r}\otimes1)\theta_{r',T}=\theta_{r,T}$. In particular the transition is $\theta_{r,T}\theta_{r',T}^{-1}$ and is invertible. For three levels, the exponent identity $\ell^{r''-r'}\ell^{r'-r}=\ell^{r''-r}$ proves composition; at equal levels the exponent is $1$. The tensors over the different finite rings are well defined because each power map is linear after restriction to the larger finite ring and $A$ factors through the smaller quotient.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product; defining power-transition formula in def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf

proof.text: For $v:T'\to T$, lem-pur-roots-of-unity-inverse-image-iso (1)-(2) says exactly that $c^v_s$ commutes with the power transitions and is semilinear over the constant finite ring maps. It also obeys identity and composition laws under the canonical inverse-image identifications: by def-pur-roots-of-unity-inverse-image its adjunct on an object $U\to T$ is the pullback of the same unit along $T'\times_TU\to U$. For $w:T''\to T'$, the iterated pullback on $T''\times_{T'}(T'\times_TU)$ is the pullback on $T''\times_TU$, because the canonical fibre-product identification commutes with the projections and pullback of global functions respects composition. Hence these adjuncts are equal, and the adjunction bijection gives $c^{v\circ w}_s=c^w_s\,w^{-1}(c^v_s)$ after the comparison isomorphism. The identity projection gives $c^{\mathrm{id}}_s=\mathrm{id}$. These are equalities of the specified maps, rather than choices of isomorphisms.

proof.text: The maps $c^v_s\,v^{-1}p_{s,T}$ form a cone by the transition equation in step 6. Apply the universal property of the limit on $T'_{\mathrm{proet}}$ to obtain $c^v_L:v^{-1}L_T\to L_{T'}$. Its projection equations are exactly those of the statement, and joint uniqueness of maps to a limit proves uniqueness. It is semilinear for the constant $\mathbf Z_\ell$ map: after $p_{s,T'}$ this says that pulling back an exponent and reducing it modulo $\ell^s$ gives the same scalar as reducing first, followed by the finite constant-ring map. This is the semilinearity in step 6 and the coordinatewise action in step 1, so the projections prove the assertion. This construction uses a cone into $L_{T'}$, never an assertion that $v^{-1}$ preserves the infinite limit.

source.place: Root inverse-limit universal property; def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit (Stacks Tags 03DB and 03CO)

proof.text: The structure maps $c^v_\Lambda:v^{-1}\Lambda_T\to\Lambda_{T'}$ of the constant coefficient rings ($\Lambda=\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathbf Z/\ell^r,A$) are the canonical ring-sheaf isomorphisms of lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image for the geometric morphism $v_{\mathrm{proet}}$; this is the identification of the statement. Apply lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor to the pro-etale geometric morphism and these constant coefficient ring maps. Together with $j_T,j_{T'}$ this identifies $v^*P_T$ with $v^{-1}L_T\otimes_{v^{-1}Z_T}A_{T'}$. The semilinear map of step 7 induces $x\otimes a\mapsto c^v_L(x)\otimes a$; this is the required $b_v$ after the stated identifications. On a pure tensor, the two sides of the required square are $p_{r,T'}c^v_L(x)\otimes a$ and $c^v_r(v^{-1}p_{r,T}(x))\otimes a$. Step 7 equates these expressions. The pure-tensor determination property gives equality of the sheaf morphisms, proving the full square with the specified root maps.

source.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback, with Tag 03EK pure tensors and the root projection equations

proof.text: For the identity morphism, every projection of $c_L^{\mathrm{id}}$ equals $p_s$, so $c_L^{\mathrm{id}}=\mathrm{id}$. For $T''\xrightarrow w T'\xrightarrow v T$, project $c_L^w\,w^{-1}(c_L^v)$ to level $s$. Using step 7 twice gives $c_s^w\,w^{-1}(c_s^v)\,(v\circ w)^{-1}p_{s,T}$ after the canonical comparison; step 6 identifies this with $c_s^{v\circ w}\,(v\circ w)^{-1}p_{s,T}$. Limit uniqueness gives the composition law for $c_L$. On a pure tensor both the composite pullback map for $b_w,w^*b_v$ and $b_{v\circ w}$ therefore send $x\otimes a$ to $c_L^{v\circ w}(x)\otimes a$. Identity and composition follow from pure-tensor determination, the canonical monoidal inverse-image comparisons, and the compatibility of the constant-ring identifications with composition of geometric morphisms stated in lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image. On the empty scheme all these formulas are the unique maps of zero sheaves. Every inverse constructed in step 4 uses only $\ell^rA=0$, so the proof imposes neither flatness over $\mathbf Z/\ell^r$ nor any divisibility of $n$ by the ramification index.

The item is not superseded (live and side-live have it unsplit), has no repair note and cites no SGA source. The statement is true: theta_r follows from p_r being an epimorphism with kernel ell^r L and from ell^r A=0, without flatness. I tested it on Spec of a separably closed field, on a ramified E with n=3 (ell^2 A=0 but ell A not 0), on the nonflat case A=F_l over Z/l^2, and on the empty scheme. It uses the constant (Z_l)_T exactly as def-coefficient-twists-detailed does, not the completed sheaf. Step checks: 2 has the correct hypotheses for lem-pur-twist-root-transitions, the general-site epi criteria and weak contractibility on the full site (Stacks 0990 proetale.tex:2913, 090K sites.tex:9480), and its recursive lift is correct. 3: the shift-division kernel calculation is correct. 4: the local-lift inverse uses lem-pur-torsion-sheaf-constant-module (2) on a slice and is correct. 5-7: the transitions, the c^v_s composition via adjuncts, and the limit cone without commuting v^-1 with the limit are correct. 8-9: the pure-tensor squares and coherence are correct. Two faults, both fixed. (1) C1: steps 8 and 9 use that the inverse image of a constant ring sheaf is the target constant ring, and its compatibility with composition, but no cited node proves it (def-weil-proetale-inverse-image only defines c^f_A). I cited lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image (closure checked, no cycle), added it to proof_deps and to split_report.tool_uses, and set step 9 to elementary=false. (2) B5: the item-level source was still Stacks 093M completion-flat applied to lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free (2), which the proof no longer uses, although the report claims it was changed.
